title: After a scam: the first hour, reporting, recovery and leading others

say: After a scam: the first hour, reporting, recovery, and leading others.
This is the video for module four: responding to fraud, reporting it and leading change.
Money moved by transfer can be passed on quickly. Do not wait.
Step one. Call the number on your ATM card. Ask them to block your card and mobile banking, contact the receiving bank, and give you a reference number.

say: Step two. Uninstall any app a scammer told you to install. Change your email password, and if your line went dead, call your network to block the SIM.

say: Step three. Screenshot chats, numbers, account names, amounts and dates. Download your statement. Save it all in one folder.

say: Step four. Report to the police, and for financial fraud, the EFCC.

say: Step five. Warn your contacts, so nobody sends money in your name. Be honest with your bank, even if you shared your OTP. Hiding it slows the investigation.

panel.rule: Do not wait until morning. Call your bank now.

say: A good report often goes to more than one agency. Always start with your bank. If it does not resolve your complaint, escalate to the Central Bank, with your reference number.

cards.d: For any money lost. Get a reference number. Unresolved? Escalate to CBN consumer protection.
Police for any fraud; EFCC for financial fraud such as advance fee fraud and Ponzi schemes.
SIM swap or scam SMS: your network, then NCC on 622. Fake pages: the platform's Report option.

say: Report to the police. Banks often ask for a police report. For financial fraud, report to the EFCC on its official website.

say: Musa lost 180,000 naira to a fake phone shop in Abuja. His report had all six parts, and he sent the same clear facts to his bank, the police and the EFCC.
Never pay anyone who offers to get your money back for a fee. That is almost always a second scam.

say: Shock, shame, anger and fear are normal after fraud. Many victims say the shame was harder than the money.

panel.heading: Self-blame or responsibility?
right: I will report it and learn

say: The scammer is responsible for the crime. You are responsible only for what you do next.
If, weeks later, you still cannot sleep, eat or work, or you feel hopeless, please talk to a doctor, a counsellor or a trusted religious leader. You do not have to carry it alone.

panel.heading: Self-blame or responsibility?

say: Bisi reported the scheme to the EFCC and SEC Nigeria, and told her landlord early. He agreed she could pay rent in two parts.

card.title: Bisi rebuilds after a Ponzi loss
card.note: Talk to creditors early. Avoid quick-fix loans.

say: She lost 400,000 naira. She cut spending and saved 40,000 a month in an account with no card. After four months she had 160,000, enough for the first part of the rent.
She avoided quick-fix loans and new investment offers, because desperation makes people open to a second scam.

say: To remember. Call your bank first, at once. Save evidence before you block. Report to the right agencies, and never pay to recover your money.
Be kind to yourself. Then turn your knowledge into protection for others.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Call your bank's official number first, at once
Save evidence before you block anyone
Report to the police, EFCC and right regulator
Never pay anyone to recover your money
Be kind to yourself, and teach others
